items.note: Component renamed (shipped as ds-auth-shell in the tagged 0.8.0 source, its only release under that name). "Shell" is not this library's word for a layout: the app-level one was renamed ds-app-shell -> ds-app-layout in 0.7.0, and calling the auth counterpart a shell put the split vocabulary back. ACTION: rename the element and its closing tag. Behaviour, inputs and slots are unchanged - brand, logoLetter, tagline, cardElevation, cardPadding, [brand], [dsBrandName] and dsAuthSupport all keep their names. Also rename the class and the tokens (separate entries below).
The exported component class renamed alongside the ds-auth-shell -> ds-auth-layout selector. Update imports and any type references. No members changed.

Prefix rename for the six component tokens: --ds-auth-shell-min-height / -card-max-width / -gap / -bg-color / -mark-bg-color / -mark-label-color -> --ds-auth-layout-*. Values and defaults are unchanged. DS-owned tokens only (no others ship under this prefix); a consumer's own --ds-auth-shell-* variable is out of scope. EXCLUDED, do not rename: the global scale token --auth-card-w, the fallback behind -card-max-width, which carries no --ds-auth-shell- prefix and keeps its name. Confirm the new name exists in the installed package.

CHANGED DEFAULT: ds-search is 40px tall at the default size, was 36px. Every size moved onto the field scale - sm var(--field-h-sm) 32px (was --hit-min 32px, unchanged), md var(--field-h-md) 40px (was --search-h 36px, CHANGED), lg var(--field-h-lg) 48px (unchanged). The old 36px was a lone tier: nothing else in the library used it, while ds-button, ds-input, ds-select and both pickers all resolve --field-h-md, so a search box in a toolbar sat 4px short of every neighbour. RESTORE the old height with `ds-search { --ds-search-height: 36px; }` - that token still wins over everything. ALSO NEW: the height now falls through --ds-field-height, so `--ds-field-height: 44px` on a toolbar levels search along with the fields, which was the point of the change.

The global --search-h token is gone; it existed only to hold ds-search's 36px and nothing reads it any more. Its replacements, in precedence order: --ds-search-height (retunes search alone) and --ds-field-height (levels the whole field family). If you declared --search-h to resize search, that declaration is now inert - swap it for --ds-search-height with the same value. Reading it in your own CSS resolves to nothing. The --hit-md scale token it pointed at (36px) is untouched and still available.

CHANGED DEFAULT: ds-table sortMode and filterMode resolve to 'server' when unset, were 'client'. An undeclared table now emits (sortChange) / updates columnFilters and reorders or filters NOTHING itself. ACTION, and it is per-table: if the table receives ALL its rows - the giveaway is that it does NOT bind `total` - add sortMode="client" and, where any column has filter: 'set', filterMode="client", or its headers will look live and do nothing. If it binds `total` it is server-paged and the new default is what you already wanted: the old 'client' sorted only the page in hand, so the rows looked sorted and were not, and a dev warning said exactly that. Tables that already declare a mode are untouched. A reversed dev warning now fires on the client case (no `total` + sortable/filterable columns + no declared mode), so run the app and let the console list them.

CHANGED DEFAULT, one size only: ds-number-stepper with size="lg" is 48px tall, was 44px. It resolved --hit-comfy while the field family's large size is --field-h-lg (--hit-touch, 48px), so a large stepper was a step short of a large input beside it. The +/- buttons and the quantity box derive their widths from that height, so they widen with it. size="sm" (32px) and the size="md" default (40px) are unchanged. RESTORE with `ds-number-stepper { --ds-field-height: 44px; }` scoped to the instance, or set the size back to md.

ds-tabs can now keep the active tab in the URL: set urlParam (e.g. urlParam="tab") and the strip writes ?tab=<name>, so the tab survives F5, a shared link and the Back button. Nothing changes until you set it, but this is worth a deliberate pass rather than a skim. ACTION, per strip: (1) GIVE EACH ds-tab A `value` if it has none - the URL is written from value, falling back to label, so without one a link carries the visible label and breaks the moment the label is translated or reworded. (2) ONE STRIP PER PARAMETER NAME. Two ds-tabs sharing a name on the same screen erase each other: both write the same query parameter, and a reload restores whichever wrote last. A dev-mode warning now names the clash. Nested or sibling strips need distinct names (tab, subtab). (3) DELETE any hand-rolled wiring - a queryParamMap subscription plus a navigate() on tabChanged is exactly what this replaces, and running both fights. Behaviour to expect: NAMES not indices (an index would silently repoint every old link as soon as a tab is inserted), the FIRST tab writes no parameter, every write uses replaceUrl so flipping tabs does not fill the Back button, and an unknown or missing name lands on the first tab instead of throwing. Inert outside a routed context, and being query-only it does not trip ds-app-layout's scroll reset.

informational: HUMAN GUIDE: migrations/unreleased/README.md walks this release in order — where to look for each change, the one call that needs judgement per table (sortMode/filterMode), and a section this project had never written before: WHAT YOU CAN NOW DELETE. Two dogfooding audits found that most consumer workarounds were written against hooks that already existed, because nothing ever told them a thing had been tokenised. Read section 3 even if the upgrade itself is clean.

NEW COMPONENT ds-field-group: several controls in one bordered box (select + input, input + button, search + date-picker). Additive, NO ACTION. If you hand-rolled a glued row by stripping borders off two controls and wrapping them, this replaces it - wrap them in <ds-field-group> and mark the stretching one with grow. Six controls can be segments: ds-input, ds-select, ds-search, ds-autocomplete, ds-date-picker, ds-button. ds-number-stepper and ds-multi-select are excluded by design. Grouped controls must not be given a label or hint - the message row would break the glued line and is suppressed.

ds-table gained [lazy] + (lazyLoad) for fetching rows as they scroll into view. Additive and opt-in, NO ACTION. If you paged a long list yourself to keep it responsive, this is the alternative: set lazy with virtualScroll and total, make data a SPARSE array total long, and write each fetched row at its ABSOLUTE index - gaps inside the window render skeleton rows. Note sortMode must not be "client" (it would sort only the rows that happen to have arrived); the new server default is already right.

--ds-field-height now reaches ds-autocomplete, ds-multi-select, ds-color-picker, ds-number-stepper, ds-split-button and the ds-modal confirm input. All six spelled their height as the raw --hit-* value, so the token the name advertises did nothing for them; they read the field scale now. Pixel-identical at every size EXCEPT ds-number-stepper at size="lg" (its own actionable entry above). NO ACTION unless you had already worked around the gap by pinning height on one of these - that pin can go.

The six connected panels (ds-select, ds-multi-select, ds-autocomplete, ds-color-picker, ds-date-picker, ds-time-picker) now build their overlay from one shared helper instead of six identical copies. Internal only, NO ACTION: the position, the 4px gap, the flip-above fallback, the panel classes and the scroll strategy are byte-for-byte what they were.

ds-autocomplete gained dsAutocompletePrefix / dsAutocompleteSuffix content slots and [showChevron] (default true). Additive, NO ACTION. If you absolutely positioned a search glyph over the field and re-padded the input, or hid the arrow with a global rule reaching for .autocomplete-chevron, replace both: put the icon in the prefix slot and set [showChevron]="false". The slot names and behaviour match ds-input's dsInputPrefix / dsInputSuffix.

ds-autocomplete gained a public clear() that empties the value AND the typed text. If you reset the field by querying the inner <input> out of the DS's DOM and dispatching a synthetic input event, delete that and call clear() on a viewChild ref - the DOM shape it depended on is not part of the public API. It deliberately does not move focus.

ds-autocomplete gained --ds-autocomplete-panel-radius (default --ds-radius-panel) and --ds-autocomplete-panel-maxh (default --picker-maxh). NO ACTION - both defaults equal today's values. The radius one matters if you square the radius roles: the autocomplete panel was the last portaled surface hard-coding --radius-lg, so it stayed rounded in an otherwise square brand. The max-height one replaces reaching for the private --picker-maxh, which ds-multi-select also reads.

ds-table gained --ds-table-head-pad-top / --ds-table-head-pad-bottom, plus showPageSize and showLabel forwarded to its footer pager. All additive with today's values as defaults, NO ACTION. Separately FIXED: density="compact" pinned padding onto the cells, which out-specified every --ds-table-*-pad-* hook, so a compact table silently ignored all of them; it now retunes the density tokens instead. Spacing is unchanged - but if you fought that with an !important, it can go.

ds-date-picker and ds-time-picker resolve their trigger's horizontal padding from --field-pad-x (new hooks: --ds-date-picker-trigger-pad-x, --ds-time-picker-trigger-pad-x) instead of a hard-coded --space-3. Identical at the default density; the difference shows under [data-density], where the token shrinks and the literal did not, leaving a picker 8px wider than the input beside it. NO ACTION unless you hand-pinned picker padding to compensate.

The ds-auth-shell -> ds-auth-layout rename is vocabulary only: no input, output, slot, token value or behaviour changed, and it is the same component 0.8.0 shipped. If you never adopted ds-auth-shell (it was added in 0.8.0), there is nothing to do.

FIXED in ds-textarea: size="sm" and size="lg" rendered the md vertical padding (12px top and bottom) regardless of the size. The size blocks set the inner textarea's vertical pad, but a :host-prefixed pin at the end of the file out-ranked them once emulated encapsulation shimmed both selectors - it carries one more attribute than the size selector. There are now three pins, one per size, and the size blocks keep only the horizontal padding they own. NO ACTION: the change is visible only on a non-md textarea and the md default is unchanged. Note that retuning --ds-input-pad-y previously moved all three sizes together; if you compensated for the wrong padding with your own override on a sm or lg textarea, that override now stacks on the corrected value and can go.

ds-auth-layout now COMPRESSES its own chrome on a short viewport: block padding, the column gap, the letter-mark tile and its glyph, the wordmark and the masthead inner gap all clamp against svh. No action - behaviour only, and a viewport 800px tall or more renders exactly what it did before, so desktop is unchanged. Below that the furniture shrinks so it is not what pushes a card into scrolling (~131px instead of ~219px at a landscape phone's ~330px). Two new tokens opt out per dimension: --ds-auth-layout-pad-block and --ds-auth-layout-mark-size; setting any of those or the existing --ds-auth-layout-gap to a fixed value stops that one compressing. A card taller than the remaining space still scrolls - that is intended.

ds-icon now logs a dev-mode warning when an icon name is in neither the DS set nor your provideDsIcons() registry - previously it rendered an empty <svg> silently. No action, and nothing changes in production. Expect the warning to surface real typos the moment you upgrade: an audit of three screens in one consumer is what prompted it.

ds-app-layout gained scrollReset: "path" | "never" | "always" (default "path" = existing behaviour, so NO ACTION), and LayoutNavigationService is now exported. If you wrote your own "did the path change?" check to work around the layout resetting scroll - or to skip a view transition, or to reset a tab - replace it with inject(LayoutNavigationService).pathChanged: it is NavigationEnd, path only, de-duplicated, and it skips a navigation carrying state: { dsSamePage: true }. Note a naive split("?") is NOT equivalent, it keeps the fragment this stream strips. To stop the layout resetting scroll on a paged or filtered list, set scrollReset="never" and call LayoutScrollService.scrollToTop() where you actually want it.

Options in ds-select / ds-autocomplete / ds-multi-select panels now have a pressed state (they had hover only, which does nothing on touch). No action - visual only. If you styled :active on .option yourself to work around it, you can drop that override; if you want a different pressed fill, it reads --surface-muted (neutral rows) and --primary-subtitle (the selected row).

ds-table gained filterMode: "client" | "server" | "none" (default "client" = existing behaviour, so NO ACTION) and columnFilterOptions. If your table is server-paged (you bind `total`) and any column has filter: "set", you WANT filterMode="server" plus columnFilterOptions with the real value domain - otherwise the checklist offers only the values on the current page and then filters locally on top of the server. A dev warning now points this out.

ds-table gained dsHeaderFilter, a template slot for a header filter the built-in checklist cannot express (date range, numeric threshold, async options). Additive, NO ACTION. If you built a host-owned popover outside the table for this, you can move it inside: <ng-template dsHeaderFilter="key" [active]="..." let-close="close">. The table keeps the button, the popover and the active styling; `active` is how you tell it your criterion is set, and `close` dismisses the panel after applying. A projected filter also makes the column filterable on its own - you do not additionally need filter: "set".

ds-table now announces sort state and row range through its role="status" region ("Sorted by Owner, ascending", "Showing 1-25 of 240"). No action - it is additive and the first render stays silent, since aria-live announces changes rather than initial content. If you added your own live region around the table for this, remove it or you will get double announcements. Wording is overridable per table through the sortAnnouncement and rangeAnnouncement inputs, which take the facts and return the sentence.

ds-table column resizing is now keyboard-operable: the handle is focusable (role="separator", labelled per column) and answers Arrow (16px), PageUp/PageDown (64px) and Home (back to automatic sizing). No action. If you hid or restyled .col-resize, note it can now receive focus and shows an indicator.

ds-table exportFetcher may now resolve a Blob or a URL string as well as rows, so a backend-formatted file downloads as-is; a new exportFailed output emits the rejection. Additive, NO ACTION - returning rows keeps working. If you wrapped the button to catch failures yourself, you can drop that.

ds-table: the FIRST column resize now freezes every visible column at its measured width before applying the drag, so untouched columns stop jumping. No action, but if you persist columnWidths (persistLayout) expect the stored map to gain entries for columns the user never dragged - that is the fix, not a bug.

ds-table sortValue string comparison now uses sensitivity: "base" alongside numeric: true, so mixed-case and accented values sort together. No action; if you relied on case-sensitive ordering, pass your own sortValue returning a normalized key.

ds-date-picker keeps its trigger indicator while the panel is open (an "open" class alongside the focus rules). Visual only, NO ACTION. If you styled .trigger:focus-within yourself to work around the trigger going dark, you can drop it.

ds-autocomplete in single mode collapses its filter input once a value is chosen and the panel is closed, so the field reads as a picker instead of a text box. Visual only, NO ACTION. Clicking the field still opens the panel and expands the input, and typing still filters. If you set --ds-autocomplete-input-minw to work around the empty box, you can drop it.

ds-date-picker: clicking the calendar glyph no longer moves focus into the day grid. It now behaves like a click on the field - with allowInput (the default) the caret stays in the field, and a read-only field still focuses the grid. No action; ArrowDown on the field enters the grid as before. If you scripted tests that assumed a glyph click lands focus on a day button, they need updating.
